title: ToolRegistryFile
description: Shape of a config/tools/*.yaml file. Validated at load time; a file that fails validation is rejected with the offending path, and hot-reload keeps the previous good version rather than half-applying.

name.description: Unique across the whole registry. snake_case. This is the name the model calls, so it must be stable — renaming it invalidates remembered experience that references it.

description.description: What the tool does AND when to reach for it, including the cases where it is the wrong choice. This text is the model's only guidance on selection, so a one-line description is a defect.

provider.description: Capability name resolved through config/providers.yaml, e.g. observability. Never a module path.

method.description: Method on the resolved provider adapter.

parameters.description: JSON Schema for the arguments, passed verbatim to the tool-calling API. Constraints belong here rather than in prose: an enum prevents an invented metric name, a maximum prevents an unbounded window.

additionalProperties.description: Must be false. Extra arguments are rejected locally rather than sent and 400'd.

permission.description: auto = runs unattended; confirm = needs per-call human approval; deny = never runs. Enforced by the policy engine before the call leaves the loop, and not overridable by the model.

retry_on.description: Only transient classes belong here. Retrying a validation error is a defect, so `validation` is not an allowed value.

idempotent.description: True when repeating the call with identical arguments is safe. The recovery ladder is allowed to blind-retry only idempotent tools.

side_effects.description: none = observes only. mutating = changes state reversibly. destructive = changes state irreversibly or with real blast radius. A `destructive` tool may not be `auto`; the loader rejects that combination.

returns.description: A short sketch of the result shape, for the model and for the docs generator.

redact.description: Field paths scrubbed before the result is logged, emitted in an event, or placed in the prompt. Redaction happens before event construction, not at serialisation.

allOf.description: A destructive tool can never be auto: unbounded blast radius must reach a human.
A deny-tier tool must not also claim retry behaviour that implies it may run.
